papers.title: The super Weil-Petersson asymptotic expansion and the coefficients
papers.abstract: We determine the universal constant in the large-genus asymptotic expansion of super Weil-Petersson volumes. The argument adopts the uniform-transport strategy for shifted theta intersection numbers. The uniform large-genus theorem for normalized BGW numbers of Guo-Norbury-Yang-Zagier determines the amplitude at a simpler endpoint. The result is $C=\pi^{-9/2}$. We give a proof of the Griguolo-Papalini-Russo-Seminara conjecture for fixed boundary lengths and fixed descendant degrees. The boundary formula is uniform when the sum of the lengths is $o(\sqrt g)$, and we exhibit an obstruction at the $\sqrt g$ scale. We also compute the first four inverse-genus coefficients by two exact recursive methods and derive general polynomial structure results. Finally, we show that, for each fixed genus, the super Weil-Petersson volume divided by $n!$ is a polynomial in the number $n$ of marked points.

papers.title: Existence of Lagrangian Mean Curvature Flow Singularities with Bounded Mean Curvature
papers.abstract: In every dimension $n \ge 3$, we show there exist Lagrangian mean curvature flows that develop neck pinch singularities such that the mean curvature remains uniformly bounded. This follows from a related result that, under a structural assumption on the singularity formation, the mean curvature at small scales near the singularity can be bounded by the Lagrangian angle at outer scales with suitable weights. Applying this result to a subset of the finite-time Lagrangian mean curvature flow singularities constructed in the companion paper [arXiv:2607.03152] and the infinite-time Lagrangian mean curvature flow singularities constructed by Tsai, Wood, and the second-named author [arXiv:2401.02228] then gives examples of both finite-time and infinite-time singularity formation with uniformly bounded mean curvature.

papers.title: Lyapunov spectrum, Harder--Narasimhan filtration and thin monodromy
papers.abstract: We study the equality case of the inequalities between the Lyapunov spectrum and the Harder--Narasimhan slopes of a semi-simple local system with non-expanding cusp monodromy over a finite-area hyperbolic surface. This gives a nonlattice-transversality alternative of the monodromy group. On the other hand, we generalize Filip's Assumptions A and B to give classes of polarized variation of Hodge structures that achieve the equality. As an application, we recover the thinness of C-32 in $\mathrm{Sp}_6\mathbb{R}$. Besides, we provide an upper bound, called average Cartan spectrum, that dominates the Lyapunov spectrum and study its rigidity.

papers.title: An ambient metric framework for sharp compactness of the constant $Q_{2N}$-curvature problem
papers.abstract: We develop a geometric method for studying $C^{2N}$-compactness of positive solutions to the constant $Q_{2N}$-curvature equation on closed Riemannian $n$-manifolds, for every integer $N\ge1$ and every dimension $n>2N$. Assuming the GJMS operator is invertible, its Green function is positive, and the positive mass condition holds, we establish sharp dimension ranges for the compactness of the set of all positive solutions with prescribed positive constant $Q_{2N}$-curvature. The largest dimension for compactness is $24$ for $N=1$ ([21]), $2N+20$ for $N=2,3$ ([11]), $2N+19$ for $N=4,5$, $2N+18$ for $N=6,7,8$, $2N+17$ for $9\le N\le17$, and $2N+16$ for all $N\ge18$. The constructions in [4,5,33,11] for $N=1,2,3$ and in the companion paper [12] for $N\ge4$ give noncompact examples in every dimension exceeding the corresponding compactness bound. We show that these $L^{\infty}$-unbounded examples can be chosen to satisfy the same operator and mass hypotheses, proving sharpness within this class. Our method relates the Pohozaev quadratic forms to the Hessian $D^2\mathscr{F}(g_c)$, where $\mathscr{F}$ is the volume-normalized total $Q_{2N}$-curvature functional and $g_c$ is the standard round metric on $\mathbb{S}^n$. The ambient metric argument of [12] supplies an explicit formula for $D^2\mathscr{F}(g_c)$ on transverse-traceless tensors. The York decomposition projects metric perturbations onto this space. The scalar--vector--tensor decomposition represents the Pohozaev quadratic forms by explicit finite-dimensional matrices. We prove that these matrices are positive definite throughout the stated dimension range, a crucial step in establishing compactness.

papers.title: Uniqueness of Ricci flows from singular initial data
papers.abstract: We establish uniqueness of Ricci flows with non-negative sectional curvatures and scaling invariant curvature bounds, assuming that the induced distance functions converge to the same initial distance function up to isometry. In the compact case, restricting the size of the initial singular set, we also establish uniqueness under suitable weaker conditions.

papers.title: Foundations on k-contact geometry
papers.abstract: $k$-Contact geometry is a generalisation of contact geometry to analyse field theories. As a main goal, we develop an approach to $k$-contact geometry based on distributions that are distributionally maximally non-integrable and admit, locally, $k$ commuting supplementary Lie symmetries: the $k$-contact distributions. More specifically, we investigate the existence of Reeb vector fields for $k$-contact distributions, $k$-contact Lie groups are defined and studied, and, after analysing compact manifolds, a Weinstein conjecture for a product of $k$ compact contact manifolds is discussed. Polarisations for $k$-contact distributions are introduced and it is shown that a polarised $k$-contact distribution is locally diffeomorphic to the Cartan distribution of the first-order jet bundle over a fibre bundle of rank $k$. We relate $k$-contact manifolds to presymplectic and $k$-symplectic manifolds on fibre bundles of larger dimension and define types of submanifolds in $k$-contact geometry. We study Hamilton--De Donder--Weyl equations on $k$-contact Lie groups. A theory of $k$-contact Hamiltonian vector fields is developed, and we describe characteristics of Lie symmetries for first-order partial differential equations in a $k$-contact Hamiltonian manner. We use our techniques to analyse Hamilton--Jacobi and Dirac equations, types of Engel and Goursat distributions, physical problems, and control systems. The work also presents introductory results so as to make it more self-contained.

papers.title: Noncompactness for the constant $Q_{2N}$-curvature problem
papers.abstract: For every integer $N\ge4$, we construct a fixed smooth, non-locally-conformally-flat metric on the $n$-dimensional unit sphere $\mathbb S^n$ for which the constant $Q_{2N}$-curvature equation admits an $L^\infty$-unbounded sequence of positive solutions. The construction applies for $n\ge2N+20$ when $N=4,5$, $n\ge2N+19$ when $6\le N\le8$, $n\ge2N+18$ when $9\le N\le17$, and $n\ge2N+17$ when $N\ge18$. For each $L \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{0\}$, the metric can be chosen arbitrarily close to the round metric in the $C^L$ norm. It can also be chosen to have a coercive GJMS operator, a strictly positive Green function, and positive Green function mass wherever the Weyl tensor and its covariant derivatives through order $\lfloor(n-2N-4)/2\rfloor$ vanish. Together with the known cases $N=1,2,3$, this establishes noncompactness at every order and proves the sharpness of the companion compactness ranges under the same operator and mass hypotheses. The construction relies on our formula for the fixed-volume Hessian of total $Q_{2N}$-curvature in transverse-traceless (TT) directions at closed Einstein metrics with $\mathrm{Ric}=(n-1)g$. For every $N \in \mathbb{N}$ and $n>2N$, this Hessian is represented by a degree-$N$ polynomial in the Lichnerowicz Laplacian, extending Matsumoto's formula for $n=2N$. For the metric perturbations generated by a fixed algebraic Weyl tensor, the quadratic reduced energy with fixed bubble center is a positive multiple of this Hessian restricted to a four-dimensional TT space. Differentiation in the bubble scale yields a finite matrix whose exact sign analysis establishes the required indefiniteness in the stated dimension ranges. After continuation to real $n$, this matrix changes from negative definite to indefinite at $n_N=2N+a_*+c_*N^{-1}+O(N^{-2})$ as $N\to\infty$, with $a_*\approx16.2018$ and $c_*\approx13.5128$, explaining the eventual bound $n\ge2N+17$.

papers.title: Compact toric Einstein four-manifolds
papers.abstract: This is a continuation of our previous paper on toric gravitational instantons. We develop a systematic theory of compact simply-connected Einstein four-manifolds with toric symmetry. Applications include (1) The construction of simply-connected positive Einstein four-manifolds with arbitrarily large $b_2$. Our method is based on local gluing combined with a global virtual counting argument. The key idea involves a particular design of rod structures to enable a gluing construction and restrict possible degenerations. (2) A topological characterization of algebraically special toric Einstein metrics in terms of $b^+_2 \leq1$. This uses special curvature identities for $W^+$ in the toric setting. (3) Uniqueness, up to scaling and isometry, of toric Einstein metrics on four-manifolds admitting an algebraically special Einstein metric. (4) Diffeomorphism classification of compact toric Einstein four-manifolds in terms of an improved Hitchin-Thorpe inequality $\chi\geq3|\tau|$. (5) Smooth compactness of simply connected toric Einstein four-manifolds with bounded Euler number. In particular, our construction recovers all the classical toric Einstein metrics, including the Page and Chen-LeBrun-Weber metrics, starting from the round sphere through moduli spaces of conical Einstein metrics.

papers.title: Uniform large-genus asymptotics of Weil-Petersson volumes
papers.abstract: Let $V_{g,n}$ be the Weil--Petersson volume of the moduli space of hyperbolic surfaces of genus $g$ with $n$ cusps. The fixed-$n$ large-genus expansion of Mirzakhani and Zograf has correction terms polynomial in $n$ of degree $2i$ at order $g^{-i}$, and is no longer asymptotically ordered by powers of $1/g$ when $n$ is of order $\sqrt g$. We prove an asymptotic expansion in powers of $1/g$, uniform in $n\ge0$. For $n\ge1$, its coefficients are analytic in a density parameter on a neighborhood of a compact interval, including the limits $n/g\to0$ and $n/g\to\infty$. Its explicit leading term contains no undetermined constant and has relative error $O(1/g)$; truncation at a sufficiently small multiple of $\sqrt g$ gives relative error $O(\mathrm{e}^{-a\sqrt g})$ for some $a>0$. For fixed $n$ this confirms Zograf's conjecture that the constant in the Mirzakhani--Zograf asymptotics is $1/\sqrt\pi$. We also determine, at every cusp density, the asymptotic profiles of the volume ratios $V_{g,n}/V_{g-1,n+2}$ and $V_{g,n+1}/(2gV_{g,n})$ and, in all degrees, the asymptotic ratios of adjacent coefficients of the one-boundary volume polynomial; this answers two questions of Mirzakhani. The proof deforms mixed $\kappa_1$--$\psi$ intersection numbers into pure $\psi$ intersection numbers along a family whose recursion has nonnegative coefficients, determines the overall constant through Painlev\'e I without assuming that the Weil--Petersson genus expansion is resurgent, and recovers individual volumes by Gaussian and Poisson coefficient extraction. As an application, the spectral gap of a Weil--Petersson random surface with $n$ cusps tends to zero in probability whenever $n/\sqrt g\to\infty$; this removes the restriction $n/g\to0$ from a theorem of Shen and Wu.

papers.title: A sharp Bernstein theorem for affine maximal type surfaces
papers.abstract: We investigate Bernstein theorem for the affine maximal type equation \begin{equation*} \sum_{i,j=1}^nf^{ij}(D^a)_{ij}=0,\qquad D=\det(f_{ij}),\qquad a\neq0, \end{equation*} under completeness of the Calabi metric. In dimension two, we prove that every smooth strictly convex solution on a convex domain is a quadratic polynomial whenever $a\notin[-\tfrac23,-\tfrac13]$, resolving a conjecture of Sun and Xu [25]. For every $n\geq2$, we also construct explicit non-quadratic Calabi complete solutions on convex domains for all $a\in[-\tfrac n{n+1},-\tfrac1{n+1}]$. These examples show that the rigidity range is sharp in dimension two.

papers.title: Iterated minimal Darboux transformations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the superposition of two minimal Darboux transformations in Euclidean three-space. A four-dimensional permutability diagram for transformations of isothermic surfaces yields the common minimal transform for distinct nonzero parameters and an explicit formula for its Gauss map. This formula determines the planar ends over regular umbilic-free points of the seed: an end is embedded when the two transformed Gauss maps coincide away from the seed value and has multiplicity 3 when all three values coincide. We illustrate this criterion with the Enneper surface and the catenoid. For the catenoid, suitable parameters give complete surfaces of finite total curvature, and we determine the numbers and multiplicities of their planar ends from the parameters and initial values. In the family with multiplicity-3 ends, the remaining initial-value parameter realizes, up to rotation, the L\'opez--Ros deformation.

papers.title: Alexandrov's theorem in the anti-Gaussian space: A Reilly-formula approach
papers.abstract: We give an alternative proof of Alexandrov's theorem about constant weighted mean curvature hypersurfaces in the anti-Gaussian space, due to the authors and Johne-Silini independently, via a Reilly-type formula approach. Moreover, we establish a sharp Heintze-Karcher-type inequality for hypersurfaces in manifolds with a generalized substatic condition, together with its rigidity in Euclidean space with density.

papers.title: On isotropic points and contact invariants of curves
papers.abstract: Let $(C_{f},0) \subset (\mathbb{C}^{n},0)$ be a germ of an irreducible holomorphic curve, given implicity by $f(x)=0$ if $n=2$ and by $f(x)=g(x)=0$ if $n=3$, and parametrised by $\gamma:(\mathbb{C},0) \rightarrow (\mathbb{C}^{n},0)$. We define the contact invariants $\operatorname{Iso}_{f}$ and $\operatorname{Iso}_{\gamma}$ for $f$ and $\gamma$, respectively, which count the number of isotropic points that appear after a generic deformation of the curve. We first consider the case where the curve is regular and establish a relation between those invariants and the number of vertices, inflection points and the zero-torsion points (for $n=3)$ that emerge from the deformation of the curve. Furthermore, we consider a germ of a singular curve with an isolated singularity and relate the number of isotropic points with the Milnor number of $f$

papers.title: Rigidity of Ricci solitons for $\varphi$-related metallic semi-Riemannian structures on para-Kenmotsu manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate Ricci solitons in the para-Kenmotsu setting with respect to a $\varphi$-related metallic semi-Riemannian metric arising from the underlying almost paracontact metric structure, under the assumption that the potential vector field is pointwise collinear with the Reeb vector field. We first establish the relation $\tS=S+2n\beta\bigl(g-\eta\otimes\eta\bigr)$ between the Ricci tensors of the original metric $g$ and the $\varphi$-related metallic metric $\tg$. We then show that the Ricci soliton equation implies that the original metric $g$ is of $\eta$-Einstein type. By combining this condition with the contracted Bianchi identity, we obtain a rigidity result implying $f=0$, $\lambda=\frac{2n}{C}$, $S=-2ng$, and consequently $\tS=-\frac{2n}{C}\tg$. Thus, every Ricci soliton in this setting whose potential vector field is pointwise collinear with the Reeb vector field is necessarily trivial, and both $g$ and $\tg$ are Einstein. Finally, we provide two five-dimensional para-Kenmotsu examples: one realizing the resulting trivial Einstein Ricci soliton and another showing that failure of the required Einstein condition prevents the existence of such a soliton.

papers.title: Perelman's entropy and Gromov-Hausdorff versus dynamical stability of round spheres
papers.abstract: We study the Gromov-Hausdorff stability of round spheres under perturbations of Perelman's nu-entropy. We show that in dimension two almost maximal entropy, together with an area normalisation, implies Gromov-Hausdorff closeness to the round two-sphere. In contrast, in dimensions at least three, we construct smooth metrics on the sphere whose entropies converge to that of the round sphere, but which remain a definite Gromov-Hausdorff distance away from it. These metrics can be chosen conformal and uniformly bi-Lipschitz equivalent to the round metric, with the same volume as the round sphere. Finally, in dimension three, we contrast this Gromov-Hausdorff instability with a dynamical stability result: metrics with nu-entropy above that of the round shrinking cylinder converge exponentially fast to round metrics under the volume-normalised Ricci flow.

papers.title: Generalised Killing Spinors and Euclidean Hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We study when the number of spinors satisfying the same generalised Killing equation for a symmetric endomorphism field $W$ forces local realisation as a Euclidean hypersurface. Let $N=2^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$ be the rank of the complex spinor bundle. We show that in dimension $n\geq4$, if the complex dimension of the solution space exceeds $N/2$, then the metric and $W$ satisfy the Gauss--Codazzi equations. This is proved in the smooth category by combining the curvature defects into a single bivector and bounding the dimension of its kernel on spinors, using algebraic curvature symmetries to handle exceptional cases. Examples obtained from non-flat four-dimensional hyperk\"ahler manifolds show that this threshold is sharp for every $n\geq4$. In dimension three, the Heisenberg group carries the maximal number of common solutions while failing the Euclidean Gauss equation. Further, in the real analytic category, we use existing extension theorems for Einstein metrics and parallel spinors to extend all common solutions to parallel spinors on a single local Ricci-flat ambient manifold. Using Wang's counts of parallel spinors, we obtain an independent proof of the sharp threshold for real analytic data.

papers.title: Filling Lipschitz spheres in metric spaces
papers.abstract: We prove a homotopical Euclidean isoperimetric inequality for Lipschitz maps from the unit n-sphere into metric spaces admitting a bounded bicombing, which includes CAT(0)-spaces and normed vector spaces. To do so, we first refine the second-named author's Euclidean isoperimetric inequality for singular Lipschitz chains to this setting. Then, we show that a singular Lipschitz chain filling induces a Lipschitz map filling of almost the same volume or less, by adapting a strategy seen in work of Gromov and others.

papers.title: Bubble Tree Convergence for Minimisers of a Regularised Baby-Skyrme Model
papers.abstract: We study degree $1$ minimisers $u: (\Sigma,g) \to S^2$ for a Baby-Skyrme model with a Sacks-Uhlenbeck regularisation term $E^{\alpha}(u) = \frac{1}{2} \int_{\Sigma} (1+\vert \nabla u \vert^2)^{\alpha+1} -1 dv_g$ and establish convergence of degree $1$ minimisers to a simple bubble tree as $\alpha \to 0$. We also obtain a new no-neck result for the classical Sacks-Uhlenbeck energy $E^{\alpha}$.

papers.title: Hodge--Riemann relations for $m$-positive and generalized $m$-positive forms
papers.abstract: We study Hodge--Riemann relations for ordinary, sequential, and weak $m$-positive real $(1,1)$-forms in complex dimension $d$. For ordinary $m$-positive forms, we prove the fully mixed relations in every permitted bidegree without assuming semipositivity, generalizing results by Xiao. As a generalization of ordinary $m$-positivity, sequential $m$-positivity is defined by the hyperbolicity cones of successive directional derivatives of the determinant. We formulate a generalized mixed Hodge--Riemann conjecture for this condition and prove several cases beyond the scalar inequalities supplied by hyperbolicity. We prove strict strong positivity for good prefixes with at most three repeated blocks after the first factor. We also consider weak $m$-positivity which corresponds to the pointwise subsolution condition for the complex $m$-Hessian equation. In this setting, we prove the Hodge--Riemann relations for $p\neq q$ and in several diagonal cases, and show that the associated power map induces a pointwise diffeomorphism onto the cone of positive $(d-1,d-1)$-forms. Using Dinh and Nguy\^en's $L^2$ globalization method, we pass from the pointwise relations to cohomology classes on compact K\"ahler manifolds. Finally, we propose conjectures on a numerical criterion for sequential positivity and on solvability of the generalized $m$-Hessian equation.

papers.title: Submersion constructions for geometries with parallel skew torsion
papers.abstract: In the absence of a de Rham decomposition theorem for geometries with torsion, we develop and unify ways to view a geometry with parallel skew torsion as the total space of a locally defined, not necessarily unique Riemannian submersion with totally geodesic fibers. We complete and extend the Cleyton-Swann classification of irreducible such geometries and characterize the cases where the stabilizer of the torsion is larger than the holonomy. As a byproduct, we obtain structure results on Gray manifolds, nearly parallel G$_2$-manifolds and Sasaki manifolds with reducible holonomy.

papers.title: Holomorphicity of parabolic stable minimal surfaces of high codimension
papers.abstract: A classical theorem of Micallef says that if $F \colon (\Sigma, g) \to \mathbb{R}^4$ is a stable minimal immersion of an oriented $2$-dimensional complete Riemannian manifold (that is parabolic) into $\mathbb{R}^4$, it is necessarily holomorphic with respect to some parallel orthogonal complex structure on $\mathbb{R}^4$. We generalize this theorem by replacing $\mathbb{R}^4$ with $\mathbb{R}^{2 + 2k}$ for any codimension $2k$, under the additional hypothesis that the normal bundle $N \Sigma$ is equipped with a complex structure that is compatible with the induced metric and parallel with respect to the induced connection. This is a necessary assumption for such a theorem to hold (as it is a consequence of the conclusion), and it is automatically satisfied in the classical case $k=1$. We also briefly discuss possible further generalizations of such a result to other calibrations and to Smith maps.

papers.title: Submanifolds of almost quaternionic skew-Hermitian manifolds
papers.abstract: We investigate several classes of submanifolds of almost quaternionic skew-Hermitian manifolds $(M^{4n}, Q, \omega)$, including almost symplectic, almost complex, almost pseudo-Hermitian and almost quaternionic submanifolds. In the torsion-free case, we realize each type of submanifold considered in the theoretical part by constructing explicit examples of submanifolds of semisimple quaternionic skew-Hermitian symmetric spaces.

papers.title: Remarks on the structure and integrability of LA-groups
papers.abstract: We study the structure of an LA-group identifying its underlying VB-group with a representation up to homotopy. We show that the Lie algebroid structure is determined by a complementary action up to homotopy of the Lie algebra of units. We identify the equations that the representation and the action need to verify in order to assemble into an LA-group, establishing an equivalence between LA-groups and LA-matched pairs. As an application, we catalog some extreme examples of representations and actions and comment on their integrability.

papers.title: Geometries with parallel, skew-symmetric and closed torsion
papers.abstract: We study Riemannian manifolds carrying a metric connection with parallel, skew-symmetric and closed torsion, which we call in short PSCT manifolds. We prove that PSCT manifolds always locally split into a product of well-understood factors, allowing a complete local classification. Further, we investigate various $G$-structures of PSCT type, with a focus on almost Hermitian structures and their possible Gray--Hervella classes.

papers.title: A Universal Obstruction to the Samuelson Condition for Tangent Lagrangian 2-Webs
papers.abstract: We study the Samuelson area condition for planar Lagrangian \(2\)-webs formed by tangent lines. For the tangent line family \(L_t:y=tx+h(t)\), where \(h\) is smooth and \(h''\neq0\), let \(\Psi(u,v)=L_u\cap L_v\) for \(u\neq v\), and let \(J_\Psi\) be its Jacobian. Domitrz and Zubilewicz (2024) proved that these webs do not satisfy the Samuelson condition. We study the Jacobian as the two tangents coalesce. In web coordinates, the Samuelson condition is equivalent to \(\partial_u\partial_v\log|J_\Psi|=0\). We show that \(J_\Psi\) has a simple zero along \(u=v\) and that \[ \partial_u\partial_v\log|J_\Psi(u,v)| =\frac{1}{(v-u)^2}+R_h(u,v), \] where \(R_h\) extends smoothly across the diagonal. The double pole therefore prevents the Samuelson condition from holding near the envelope. We also give a direct local proof of this failure for webs formed by two separated smooth line families with varying slopes.

papers.title: Dolbeault cohomology of Endo-Pajitnov manifolds
papers.abstract: Endo-Pajitnov manifolds are compact non-K\"ahler manifolds which generalize the Inoue surfaces $S_M$ to higher dimensions. In this paper, we compute their Dolbeault cohomology, show that they satisfy the Hodge decomposition at the level of dimensions and prove that they are rigid with respect to small deformations.

papers.title: Holomorphic functions on complete Hermitian manifolds with flat Chern connection
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove several results concerning the function theory of complete Hermitian manifolds with vanishing Chern curvature, which we refer to as complete Chern-flat manifolds. First, we show that any complete simply connected Chern-flat manifold is elliptic in the sense of Gromov. Moreover, it is biholomorphic to a complex Lie group if the torsion has polynomial growth. We also construct examples of complete Chern-flat manifolds with torsion of exponential growth, but the underlying complex manifolds do not admit any complex Lie group structures. Next, we obtain sharp upper bounds on the dimensions of holomorphic functions of polynomial growth on complete Chern-flat manifolds, without any growth assumption on the torsion. Finally, we prove that any complete Chern-flat manifold admitting polynomial-growth holomorphic functions that form a local holomorphic coordinate system at some point is biholomorphic to complex Euclidean space. These results generalize our previous work, where we assume that the torsion has sublinear growth. Our approach combines Cauchy estimates with nilpotent analysis along the orbits of holomorphic flows generated by parallel unitary frames on such manifolds.

papers.title: On $(2,1)$-dimensional anti-de Sitter spacetimes with convex boundary
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be a closed oriented surface of genus at least $2$. Let $X$ be a $(2,1)$-dimensional anti-de Sitter spacetime homeomorphic to $S\times[-1,1]$ with smooth, spacelike, strongly convex boundary. By Gauss' formula, the induced metric on each of the two components of $\partial X$ has curvature $K<-1$. In this paper we address the inverse problem. We show that, for any two smooth metrics $h_-, h_+$ on $S$ with curvature $K<-1$, there exists a unique, smooth anti-de Sitter metric on $X:=S\times [-1,1]$ with respect to which the boundary is locally strongly convex and has induced metric isotopic to $h_-$ on its past component and isotopic to $h_+$ on its future component. Existence has already been proven by Tamburelli. We use this result to solve affirmatively a conjecture of Mess: given any two measured laminations $l_-, l_+\in\mathcal{ML}_S$ that together fill $S$, there exists a unique $(2,1)$-dimensional, globally hyperbolic, maximal, Cauchy compact (GHMC) anti-de Sitter spacetime such that the measured bending laminations of the past and future boundary components of its convex core are respectively $l_-$ and $l_+$. Here, existence has already been proven by Bonsante--Schlenker.

papers.title: Schwarz $\mathrm{P}$ and Schwarz $\mathrm{D}$ as free-boundary minimal disks in a tetragonal disphenoid: exact areas
papers.abstract: Let $T$ be the tetragonal disphenoid whose four congruent faces are isosceles triangles with sides $2,\sqrt3,\sqrt3$, so that the dihedral angles are $\pi/2$ along one opposite pair of edges and $\pi/3$ along the remaining four. By Smyth's theorem $T$ contains three embedded minimal disks meeting $\partial T$ orthogonally; the symmetry group $D_{2d}$ of $T$ fixes one and interchanges the other two. We identify all three completely. The distinguished disk is a patch of $\textbf{Schwarz's $\mathrm{P}$ surface}$ and the congruent pair are patches of $\textbf{Schwarz's $\mathrm{D}$ surface}$, with exact areas \[ \operatorname{Area}(\Sigma^{*}_{A}) = \frac{K\!\left(\tfrac14\right)} {K\!\left(\tfrac34\right)} = 0.781700961348056\ldots, \] \[ \operatorname{Area}(\Sigma^{*}_{B}) = \frac{K\!\left(\tfrac34\right)} {2\,K\!\left(\tfrac14\right)} = 0.639630785585503\ldots \] in the normalization $\operatorname{Vol}(T)=2/3$, inradius $r_T=\sqrt2/4$. In particular $2\,\operatorname{Area}(\Sigma^{*}_{A})\operatorname{Area}(\Sigma^{*}_{B})=1$, which we show is the Bonnet relation for the adjoint pair $(\mathrm{D},\mathrm{P})$. The proof is a reversal of the usual strategy: rather than uniformizing the Gauss map, we identify Smyth's three Plateau contours as the $\textit{tetrahedral four edges}$ and the $\textit{octahedral four edges}$ --- classically solved by $\mathrm{D}$ and $\mathrm{P}$ respectively --- and then conjugate. Both areas agree with Surface Evolver computations of Ken Brakke to all $15$ reported digits. We also show that all twelve corners of the three disks are midpoints of edges of $T$, each of the six midpoints being used twice, and that $T$ is precisely the alcove of the affine Weyl group $\widetilde{A}_{3}$, confirming a remark of Gandy, Cvijovi\'c, et al. (1999).

papers.title: Riemannian convex bodies with a boundary geodesic segment
papers.abstract: We construct compact convex bodies whose boundaries contain a nontrivial geodesic segment and are strictly convex elsewhere. The construction applies if sectional curvature is constant near a point, or if a normal Jacobi operator has a simple maximal eigenvalue. This implies existence of such bodies in any three-dimensional manifold. A further argument to show existence in dimension four.
